title: Rust: accounting restart and restore lifecycle
description:
Connect active airtime restrictions in rust/lichen-core/src/duty_cycle.rs to existing storage interfaces in rust/lichen-hal/src/storage.rs and initialization in rust/lichen-node/src/stack.rs. Restore valid restrictions or conservatively wait out their window. Reboot, reconnect, wall-clock corrections and unknown downtime must not create a fresh allowance for a physical resource.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Prefer the minimum existing-storage integration or conservative wait-out needed for correctness; no generic persistence framework or new dependency is required. Accounting state must remain distinct from schedule generations, link replay and identity portability. Do not edit key export/import or audited OSCORE/EDHOC state/security semantics. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil identity, radio ownership, baseline SCHC and best-effort custody.
acceptance_criteria: Drive vectors.09 restart traces through production lifecycle APIs with independently specified elapsed-time and interval outcomes. Fault-inject missing/corrupt records, failed persistence, unknown downtime and clock changes; verify TX remains denied until the correct boundary. Exercise both successful restoration and conservative wait-out without using the tracker to calculate expected values. Run targeted core/HAL/node tests, applicable no-default-feature checks, fmt and clippy.
